content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm encountering difficulty activating HTTPS for the webserver on my [product_name]. I'm using [product_name] V8.3.0, but when I access the settings tab, there isn’t an option to enable HTTPS for the webserver. My [product_name] is [article_no] with firmware [version_no]. Any guidance on what I might be missing would be greatly appreciated.
HTTPS support is only available in [product_name] V8.3, not in V8.2. Access control settings differ between these versions. Both screenshots shown use [product_name] V8.3.
That seems inconsistent. The [article_no] model is actually a [product_name] V8.2, and typically comes with firmware version V1.82.x. Firmware version V1.80.2 is not listed.
Thank you for the clarification. I likely misread the firmware version. If HTTPS is necessary, do I need to obtain a new [product_name], or is it possible to update my current one?
It is not possible to upgrade the firmware to V1.83.x (which is required for [product_name] V8.3 firmware).

analysis.insight_summary: A user is trying to enable HTTPS for the webserver on their [product_name], but learns that their current device and firmware do not support this feature. The exchange clarifies differences in feature availability across hardware and firmware versions, and points out confusion caused by inconsistent version references.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates enabling HTTPS on their [product_name] using standard configuration software and hopes for an upgrade path if limitations exist due to hardware or firmware constraints.
